text.p: Hollywood Entertainment Corp plans to accelerate its expansion, with 256 new video rental stores opening this year and 300 next year for a total of 1,000 stores by 1998, Chairman Mark Wattles said.
He also said that the company will need additional financing to fund this expansion.

"Our capital needs are fine until the end of this year," Wattles told the Montgomery Securities Investment Conference. He said he anticipates needing additional capital of $90 million in 1997 and $70 million in 1998 to keep its planned expansion on line.
Wattles gave no specific projections for growth beyond 1998, other than to say "we see the potential for 2,000 stores in the U.S."
Despite those ambitions, he said the company's strategy was not to take market share from Blockbuster Video, the largest video rental chain in the U.S.
"The industry is still highly fragmented," he said, explaining that 74 percent of the market was held by small, mostly local and non-public operations.
"Blockbuster will probably continue to grow and expand, but there is plenty of room for another (major player). It's that 74 percent of the market that we are after."
Hollywood Entertainment is the second largest video rental store in the U.S., after Blockbuster.
Blockbuster is a unit of Viacom Inc.
